answer: Behavioral Graph Clustering Isolation Nodes clustering within a tight interaction grove share abnormal synchronicity. The network inspects temporal transaction graphs post-facto. When isolated clusters exhibit identical coordination patterns exceeding statistical thresholds, automated pruning severs their access vine. Attackers pay a direct compute and capital penalty: every sybil node caught in the dense subgraph forfeits accumulated utility and locked rewards, turning bulk duplication into a net-negative yield exercise that bleeds capital like cracked jade.
